programme.title: Murder on the Victorian Railway
programme.desc: London 1864. On a Hackney-bound train, a guard discovers blood in a first-class carriage - and a body on the railway embankment. For the first time, a murder has taken place on Britain's railways. Over a hundred years later, this documentary uses the first-hand testimony of the people involved at the time to explore this unique event and how it provoked a huge public outcry and debate.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.sub-title: How to Write a Mills and Boon
programme.desc: To mark 100 years of romance publishers Mills and Boon, literary novelist Stella Duffy takes on the challenge of writing for them. Romantic fiction is a global phenomenon, and Mills and Boon are among the biggest names in the business. The company welcomes submissions from new authors, but as Duffy soon finds out, writing a Mills and Boon is harder than it looks.

programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: Marilyn Monroe's story is told through the insights and anecdotes of friends, directors and fellow actors who spoke about her over the years on a selection of BBC programmes.

programme.title: Some Like It Hot
programme.desc: Joe and Jerry are two innocent musicians who accidentally witness a gangland murder. To get out of town in a hurry and be paid for it, they disguise themselves as women, and join an all-girl band travelling to Florida. All seems to be going well until Joe, as Josephine, starts to fall for Sugar Kane, the band's singer, and Jerry, as Daphne, elicits more interest than he'd like from millionaire Osgood Fielding III.

programme.title: Nobody's Perfect: The Making of Some Like It Hot
programme.desc: Revealing documentary about the creation and shooting of the acclaimed comedy movie. Including interviews with stars Jack Lemmon and Tony Curtis and behind-the-scenes colour footage.

programme.title: My Week With Marilyn
programme.desc: Colin Clark works as an assistant on the set of the Laurence Olivier and Marilyn Monroe film 'The Prince and the Showgirl'. When Arthur Miller, Monroe's playwright husband, leaves the country, Clark introduces Monroe to British life in a week in which she escapes from her Hollywood routine and the pressures of stardom.

programme.title: Art of Scandinavia
programme.desc: In the final instalment of Andrew Graham-Dixon's windswept journey through the art of the Norselands, we arrive in Sweden - home of IKEA and a tradition of brilliant furniture design stretching back to the early years of the 20th century. Sweden has made its modern democratic mission one of comfort and civilised living for the masses.

programme.title: Miles Davis: Birth of the Cool
programme.desc: The central theme of Miles Davis's life was his restless determination to break boundaries and live life on his own terms. It made him a star. It also made him incredibly difficult to live with for the people who loved him most.

programme.title: Drama Intros
programme.desc: Alan Yentob shares the fascinating story of how a 1974 broadcast of the great Ella Fitzgerald singing in Ronnie Scott's nightclub came about. A tale of tenacity, Alan recounts how he managed to persuade Ella's manager to let the BBC film.

programme.title: Ella Fitzgerald's Other Show

programme.title: Cleo Laine at the BBC
programme.desc: A special celebration of Dame Cleo Laine's finest moments on the BBC to coincide with her ninety-fifth birthday. Britain's 'First Lady of Jazz' became a star after joining The John Dankworth Seven in the 1950s and then marrying the bandleader.

programme.title: Jazz 625 at the BBC
programme.desc: A look through the archive of the legendary BBC Jazz concert show from the mid-60s. Featuring classic performances from legends such as Duke Ellington, Dave Brubeck, Dizzy Gillespie and The Julian 'Cannonball' Adderley Sextet.
